idea-plugin.name: Claude Terminal Tab Persistence
idea-plugin.description:
Claude Terminal Tab Persistence for Rider / IntelliJ

Auto-restores your Claude Code terminal sessions across IDE restarts. The plugin tracks alive Claude sessions in ~/.claude/rider-plugin/active-sessions/ and, on next project open, spawns one fresh terminal tab per saved session running claude --resume <sid>.

3.0 redesign — own the terminal

The plugin now creates every Claude tab itself and assigns its session id at launch, so tab ↔ session identity is a stored fact from birth — no reflection, ancestry walks, or title guessing. Openness is simply "the tab is present in the tool window"; only an × closes a tab, while window-close, quit, crash, and reboot all reopen every open tab.

  • The plugin owns Claude tab titles. Every tab hosting a Claude session shows ✳ <name>, and the glyph animates while the session is thinking (mirroring Claude's own busy/idle status). Titles are continuously enforced — a tab clobbered to "Local" self-heals within half a second.
  • Names that stick. Display name priority: your explicit name (Rider's "Rename Tab" or /tab) > Claude's auto-generated topic name > the cached topic. Renames are adopted and persisted across restarts, never fought.
  • One file per alive session. active-sessions/<sid>.json — race-safe, no per-project file conflicts.
  • Bounded eviction backlog. session-backlog.json keeps the last 50 evicted sessions so you can recover them with /tabs-history.

Slash Commands

  • /tab — set this session's tab name explicitly (persists across restarts)
  • /tabs-status — live sessions + recent eviction backlog for the current project
  • /tabs-backup — explicit sync: write per-sid files for every alive Claude process
  • /tabs-history — browse the eviction backlog and print a resume command
  • /tabs-restore — list current per-sid files and print resume commands
  • /tabs-clear — clear active-sessions/ for the current project

Requirements: Rider / IntelliJ 2026.1+, Claude Code CLI, Node.js (for the bundled helper scripts).

Coexists with the JetBrains AI Assistant chat tool window (AI Agents panel: Junie / Claude Agent / Codex) and Anthropic's official Claude Code [Beta] plugin. This plugin manages terminal-launched Claude CLI sessions only — chat tabs in the AI Agents panel are managed by JetBrains.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
3.1.2 — open tabs can no longer go invisible to the plugin

  • Fixes sessions silently missing from restore after a long IDE session. The terminal plugin caches its tool-window reference once; when the IDE re-creates the Terminal tool window that cached reference points at an empty, disposed window. The plugin enumerated tabs through it, saw none, and so never recorded any tab as open — after the next restart nothing came back, even though the tabs had been visibly open for days. Tabs are now read from the IDE's tool-window registry (including split groups) and cross-checked against the terminal's own tab list; a stale cache is logged as a warning instead of silently emptying the restore snapshot.

3.1.1 — hand-opened Claude tabs are adopted again

  • A tab you typed claude or claude --resume <id> into is picked up again on the reworked terminal. It binds to the session, gets renamed, honors /tab, and comes back after a restart — previously such a tab was never adopted and its session was silently absent from the restore snapshot.
  • Tabs are identified by facts, not guesses. A terminal tab now reports the command line it was launched with, the process id at its root, and its launch directory. Two exact rules follow: a tab whose launch command names a session is that session, and a session whose process descends from a tab's root process is running in that tab — which is precisely the hand-typed case. Neither rule needs the tab's title, its working directory, or the order tabs were opened in.
  • Plain shell tabs never receive a session by guesswork. A tab that looks like a bash / PowerShell prompt is excluded from the order- and directory-based matching passes — it can neither be given a session nor stand in the way of the real Claude tab getting one. (The two exact rules above are exempt: a tab proven to host a session is bound whatever it is called.) Ambiguity still refuses, in both directions, and a pre-existing tab can no longer absorb a session id minted for a newly launched one.

3.1.0 — WSL session roots

  • Windows and WSL Claudes are now cleanly separated — and both supported. Each running WSL distro's ~/.claude is tracked as its own session root: a separate installation, typically a separate account. Sessions are titled/animated from their own root's status, and restore launches through the owning root (wsl.exe -d <distro> … claude --resume vs plain claude --resume), so a session always comes back under the account it belongs to. A sleeping distro never costs a tab — resuming boots it.
  • Stale sessions can no longer steal fresh tabs. Adopting a session onto a hand-opened tab now requires the session's process to be minutes old (the legitimate "just typed claude" case) — a long-running orphan can't grab a new empty tab, wear its name and animation, or leak identity across roots.
  • Startup terminals are plugin-authored only. The IDE terminal's own tab persistence reopened tabs and re-ran their commands — an IDE-restored claude tab spawned a brand-new empty session next to the plugin's resumed one (duplicate "Claude" tabs after every restart). The persisted tab list is now cleared at shutdown. A one-time notification explains the takeover with a one-click opt-out (also: rider.claude.tabs.ownStartupTabs registry key). Uninstalling or disabling the plugin automatically returns the IDE's own behavior — the takeover is a per-shutdown action, never a persistent settings change.

3.0.1 — Marketplace compliance

No internal platform API: quit detection now rides the public app-lifecycle listener (same snapshot-freeze semantics). Plugin classloader lookup moved off the deprecated accessor. The remaining deprecated terminal calls are deliberate — their official replacements are still marked experimental on every supported platform build.

3.0.0 — Own the terminal

Ground-up rewrite. The plugin creates every Claude tab itself and assigns its session id at launch — tab ↔ session identity is a stored fact, never guessed. Only an × closes a tab; window-close, quit, crash, and reboot restore every open tab, named and animated, in order. Real topic names win over placeholders and launcher defaults, transient tool titles are never captured, shell tabs are never mis-bound, and the plugin never kills a process.

2.0.0

Per-session files with crash-atomic writes, eviction backlog, title ownership + thinking animation. Superseded by 3.0.

1.0.18

Heuristic identity matching (ancestry walks, window-state serialization). Superseded.

registryKey.description: Defer to JetBrains AI Assistant / Anthropic Claude Code plugin when present (informational log only).

Clear the IDE terminal's own tab persistence at shutdown so every startup terminal tab is plugin-authored. Prevents IDE-restored tabs from re-running claude as brand-new empty sessions next to the plugin's resumed ones. Disable to get the IDE's own shell-tab restore back.

action.description: Open a new Claude Code session in a plugin-owned terminal tab (durable across restarts).
